title: Error: unable to find user app: no matching entries in passwd file
body:
### Issue Description

Tyring to login into existing container causing the error: Error: unable to find user app: no matching entries in passwd file

But user exists inside container /etc/passwd file.

```
# podman exec -it --user app cont1 bash
Error: unable to find user app: no matching entries in passwd file
# podman exec -it --user 0 cont1 grep app /etc/passwd
app:x:1000:1000::/app:/bin/sh
```

Happens because of side effect of running build command

```
echo "FROM alpine" | podman build --log-level=debug -t "test" -f - .
```

### Steps to reproduce the issue

1.

```
podman build -t test1 -f - . << EOF
FROM ubuntu:latest
RUN useradd -m app
USER app
EOF
```

2. mkdir 123
3. podman run -d --name t1 --replace --userns=keep-id -v "$(pwd)/123:/tmp:Z,U" test1 sleep 60
4. podman exec -it --user app t1 echo # fine
5. open another terminal and complete `second terminal step`.
6. sleep 5
7. podman exec -it t1 echo # error

`second terminal step`:

```
podmanenv() {
  local PODMAN_HOME="$PWD/podman"
  export CONTAINERS_STORAGE_CONF="$PODMAN_HOME/storage.conf"
  mkdir -p "$PODMAN_HOME"
  cat << EOF > "$CONTAINERS_STORAGE_CONF"
[storage]
driver = "overlay"
runroot = "$PODMAN_HOME"
graphroot = "$PODMAN_HOME"
rootless_storage_path = "$PODMAN_HOME"
EOF
  export TMPDIR="$PODMAN_HOME/tmp"
  mkdir -p "$TMPDIR"
}

podmanenv
echo "FROM alpine" | podman build --log-level=debug -t "test" -f - .
```

### Describe the results you received

An error on 7 step: `Error: unable to find user app: no matching entries in passwd file`

### Describe the results you expected

same result on step 4 and step 7

comments.body:
We only support the latest version upstream so please test with the latest podman again.

In general I don't quite follow what you are doing here with the second terminal that should really not affect the former but the setup you are doing there looks invalid in any case, runroot and graphroot must not be the same.

The only thing I could see is that the rootless user namespace gets messed up due this.
Compare `podman unshare readlink /proc/self/ns/user` before and afterwards

Here is a single script you can run on any environment you would like to test the issue:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -e

echo "=== 0. Подготовка окружения и очистка старых следов ==="
podman rm -f t1 >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
rm -rf 123 podman

echo "=== 1. Сборка базового образа test1 с пользователем app ==="
podman build -t test1 -f - . << 'EOF'
FROM ubuntu:latest
RUN useradd -m app
USER app
EOF

echo "=== 2. Создание директории для монтирования ==="
mkdir -p 123

echo "=== 3. Запуск контейнера t1 с флагом --userns=keep-id ==="
podman run -d --name t1 --replace --userns=keep-id -v "$(pwd)/123:/tmp:Z,U" test1 sleep 60

echo "=== 4. Проверка работы до бага (Ожидается: Успех) ==="
if podman exec -it --user app t1 echo ">>> Шаг 4: Успешно зашли под пользователем app"; then
    echo "Шаг 4 выполнен без ошибок."
else
    echo "Ошибка на шаге 4!"
    exit 1
fi

podman unshare readlink /proc/self/ns/user

echo "=== 5 & 6. Эмуляция действий во втором терминале ==="
echo "Выполняем сборку другого образа с измененными переменными хранилища..."
mkdir -p secondstep
(
    cd secondstep
    PODMAN_HOME="$PWD/podman"
    export CONTAINERS_STORAGE_CONF="$PODMAN_HOME/storage.conf"
    mkdir -p "$PODMAN_HOME"
    mkdir -p "$PODMAN_HOME/1"
    mkdir -p "$PODMAN_HOME/2"

    cat << 'EOF' > "$CONTAINERS_STORAGE_CONF"
[storage]
driver = "overlay"
runroot = "$PODMAN_HOME/1"
graphroot = "$PODMAN_HOME/2"
rootless_storage_path = "$PODMAN_HOME"
EOF

    export TMPDIR="$PODMAN_HOME/tmp"
    mkdir -p "$TMPDIR"

    # Запускаем сборку, которая ломает пространство имен
    echo "FROM alpine" | podman build -t "test" -f - . > /dev/null 2>&1
)

echo "Ожидаем 5 секунд (шаг 6)..."
sleep 5

podman unshare readlink /proc/self/ns/user

echo "=== 7. Проверка работы ПОСЛЕ бага (Ожидается: Ошибка passwd) ==="
set +e # Отключаем немедленный выход при ошибке, чтобы скрипт показал финальный статус
podman exec -it --user app t1 echo ">>> First Try"
podman unshare readlink /proc/self/ns/user
podman exec -it --user app t1 echo ">>> Second Try"
EXIT_CODE=$?
podman unshare readlink /proc/self/ns/user

echo "========================================="
if [ $EXIT_CODE -ne 0 ]; then
    echo "❌ Воспроизведение успешно! Шаг 7 упал с кодом $EXIT_CODE."
else
    echo "🎉 Ошибка НЕ воспроизвелась. Шаг 7 прошел успешно."
fi

# Очистка (раскомментируйте, если нужно удалять автоматически)
podman rm -f t1 >/dev/null 2>&1
sudo rm -rf 123 podman secondstep
```

root cause: shared rootless runroot corrupts mountpoints.json

## Environment

- Debian 13 (trixie), kernel 6.12, cgroup v2, systemd 257
- podman 5.4.2+ds1-2+b2 (containers/storage v1.57.2)
- buildah 1.39.3+ds1-1+b7
- crun 1.21
- Rootless, user uid 1000, `/etc/subuid` configured, `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1000`
- Reproduced with the exact single-shell script from the issue, run as the rootless user
  (not root, not via a separate terminal).

## Summary

The error is not caused by a broken user namespace. It is caused by a **shared
rootless `runroot`** between the default store and the store created through
`CONTAINERS_STORAGE_CONF`. Both stores end up using the same
`/run/user/1000/containers/overlay-layers/mountpoints.json`. The alternate-store
build rewrites that file with only its own layers (ultimately `[]`), erasing the
record of the running container's mounted layer. The next default-store command
then believes nothing is mounted, calls `overlay.Cleanup()`, and lazily unmounts
the store's overlay-home bind mount. Because rootless commands run in the pause
process's mount namespace, this detaches the container's `merged` mount too. The
following `podman exec --user app` cannot open `<mountpoint>/etc/passwd` and
moby/sys/user reports that missing file as "no matching entries in passwd file".

The container itself keeps running; only the host/pause view of its merged
rootfs is gone. That is why `--user 0` still works and `podman ps` still shows
the container as Up.

## Reproduction (exact issue script)

```bash
export XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1000
cd /home/a/issue30006

podman build -t test1 -f - . <<'EOF'
FROM ubuntu:latest
RUN useradd -m app
USER app
EOF

mkdir -p 123
podman run -d --name t1 --replace --userns=keep-id \
  -v "$(pwd)/123:/tmp:Z,U" test1 sleep 600

podman exec -it --user app t1 echo ">>> step 4 OK"   # works

# second store, as in the issue
mkdir -p secondstep && cd secondstep
PODMAN_HOME="$PWD/podman"
export CONTAINERS_STORAGE_CONF="$PODMAN_HOME/storage.conf"
mkdir -p "$PODMAN_HOME" "$PODMAN_HOME/1" "$PODMAN_HOME/2" "$PODMAN_HOME/tmp"
cat > "$CONTAINERS_STORAGE_CONF" <<EOF
[storage]
driver = "overlay"
runroot = "$PODMAN_HOME/1"
graphroot = "$PODMAN_HOME/2"
rootless_storage_path = "$PODMAN_HOME"
EOF
export TMPDIR="$PODMAN_HOME/tmp"
echo "FROM alpine" | podman build -t test -f - .

podman exec -it --user app t1 echo ">>> step 7"      # fails
# Error: unable to find user app: no matching entries in passwd file
```

Important: the script must be run as the rootless user in one shell. Running it as
root changes the store involved and does not reproduce.

## Why the alternate `runroot`/`graphroot` do not take effect on 5.4.2

With the config above, `podman info` reports:

    graphRoot = /home/a/issue30006/secondstep/podman
    runRoot   = /run/user/1000/containers

So the configured `runroot = $PODMAN_HOME/1` and `graphroot = $PODMAN_HOME/2`
are ignored; only `rootless_storage_path` survives. In containers/storage
v1.57.2 `types/options.go`:

- `loadDefaultStoreOptions()` reads `CONTAINERS_STORAGE_CONF` into
  `defaultStoreOptions`, but does not set `defaultConfigFile` to that path.
- `loadStoreOptionsFromConfFile()` calls `getRootlessStorageOpts()`, which
  unconditionally overwrites `RunRoot`:
  `opts.RunRoot = filepath.Join(rootlessRuntime, "containers")` (~line 303).
- Because `/etc/containers/storage.conf` exists, it then reloads only the system
  file, discarding the alternate file's `runroot`/`graphroot`. `graphroot`
  falls back to `rootless_storage_path`, which *was* propagated by
  `getRootlessStorageOpts`.

Result: both stores use the same runroot, hence the same
`overlay-layers` directory and the same `mountpoints.json`.

Relevant paths derived from `runroot`:

- overlay home: `runhome := filepath.Join(options.RunRoot, filepath.Base(home))`
  (drivers/overlay/overlay.go:324) -> `/run/user/1000/containers/overlay`
- layer store run dir: `rlpath := filepath.Join(s.runRoot, driverPrefix+"layers")`
  (store.go:1137) -> `/run/user/1000/containers/overlay-layers`
- mount registry: `filepath.Join(r.rundir, "mountpoints.json")`
  (layers.go:772-773)

## The failure sequence

1. `podman run` starts t1. `mountpoints.json` contains t1's layer:

       [{"id":"<layer-id>","path":".../<layer-id>/merged","count":1}]

   The pause namespace has the overlay-home bind mount and the container's
   `merged` mount (both count 1).

2. The alternate-store build loads that file. `loadMounts()` only applies
   records whose ID exists in the *local* store (layers.go:977-988), so t1's
   entry is ignored. On save, `saveMounts()` serialises only the current
   store's layers with `MountCount > 0` (layers.go:1065+) -> writes `[]`.

   The mounts remain attached; only the bookkeeping is lost.

3. Any subsequent default-store command (`podman ps`, `podman inspect`,
   `podman exec`, or the issue script's `podman unshare` in `pausestate`)
   loads `[]`. t1's layer now has `MountCount == 0`, so `store.Shutdown()`
   sees no mounted layers and calls `graphDriver.Cleanup()`
   (store.go:3598, 3652). `overlay.Cleanup()` does
   `mount.Unmount(d.home)` -> `unmount(<graphroot>/overlay, MNT_DETACH)`
   (overlay.go:860-865).

4. Rootless commands join the pause process's user and mount namespaces
   (`reexec_userns_join` -> `setns(user)`, `setns(mnt)` in
   `pkg/rootless/rootless_linux.c:583,589`). The unmount therefore happens in
   the namespace that also holds the container's `merged` mount, so `merged`
   disappears with the overlay-home bind mount.

5. `podman exec --user app` calls
   `lookup.GetUserGroupInfo(c.state.Mountpoint, "app", nil)`
   (libpod/oci_conmon_exec_common.go:718). The lookup opens
   `<mountpoint>/etc/passwd`. `moby/sys/user.GetExecUserPath` silently ignores
   the `os.Open` failure (user.go:257) and passes a nil reader to
   `GetExecUser`, which returns `ErrNoPasswdEntries` (user.go:357), wrapped as:

       unable to find user app: no matching entries in passwd file

## Evidence

`mountpoints.json` before/after the alternate build:

    before: [{"id":"5b1d8b...","path":".../5b1d8b.../merged","count":1}]
    after:  []

Pause mount namespace (counts of the overlay home and of
`<graphroot>/overlay/<id>/merged`):

    before podman ps: db_home=1 merged=1
    after  podman ps: db_home=0 merged=0

strace of that plain `podman ps` (default store, read-only command):

    setns(7, 0) = 0
    setns(8, 0) = 0
    umount2("/home/a/.local/share/containers/storage/overlay", MNT_DETACH) = 0

Exec results in the broken state:

    podman exec --user app t1 ...  -> rc=255
      Error: unable to find user app: no matching entries in passwd file
    podman exec --user 0  t1 id    -> rc=0   uid=0(root) ...

The container is still running:

    podman ps -> t1 Up
    payload pid's mount namespace: overlay mounted at /
    /proc/<pid>/root/etc/passwd still contains "app:x:1000:..."
    host <merged>/etc/passwd: ENOENT; <merged> is empty

Other checks:

- The user namespace inode does not change (`user:[4026532536]` before/after);
  `podman unshare readlink /proc/self/ns/user` is stable. The user namespace
  is not the problem.
- A default-store build after t1 runs does not corrupt the registry, because
  its layer list still includes t1's layer.
- Read-only alternate-store commands (`podman info`, `podman images`) do not
  call `saveMounts()`, so they do not corrupt it.
- Therefore the minimal trigger is a *build in a different store that shares
  the default store's runroot*.

## Why the reported details look odd

- `--user 0` works because numeric UIDs need no passwd entry; the broken file
  is never read.
- The container stays Up because the payload process has its own mount
  namespace with the overlay at `/`. Only the pause/host view of `merged` is
  detached.
- The first exec sometimes succeeds and the second fails: the detach happens
  at the *shutdown* of the next default-store command. In the issue script,
  `pausestate` runs `podman unshare` between the build and step 7, so the
  detach happens before the first exec and both fail.
- `podman restart` fails with the same user-lookup error (rc 125);
  `podman system migrate` stops/kills the container (`Exited (137)`). Neither
  recovers the container.

## Status on current main

Current main (go.podman.io/storage v1.65.x) parses `CONTAINERS_STORAGE_CONF`
directly and honors `storage.runroot` / `storage.graphroot`
(types/options.go:224-249). With the issue's config (explicit
`runroot=$PODMAN_HOME/1`), the alternate store gets its own
`overlay-layers/mountpoints.json`, so the exact reproducer likely no longer
fails there.

The underlying hazard is still present:

- `runhome = RunRoot/basename(home)` and `rlpath = RunRoot/overlay-layers`
  are unchanged (overlay.go:341, store.go:1191).
- `saveMounts()` still drops records for layers not in the current store
  (layers.go:1244).
- `Shutdown()` still calls `Cleanup()` when no layer is marked mounted, and
  `Cleanup()` still unmounts `d.home` (overlay.go:907-912).
- Two stores that share a runroot (for example an alternate config that omits
  `runroot` and inherits `/run/user/<uid>/containers`) can still corrupt each
  other.

## Suggested fixes

1. Make the mount registry per-store rather than per-runroot, or key entries
   by store identity and merge on write instead of replacing the file with
   only the current store's layers.
2. Do not unmount the driver home based on incomplete mount state.
   `overlay.Cleanup()` detaching `d.home` from a short-lived command is
   dangerous; it should only remove mounts owned by the current store/process,
   or the registry must be authoritative.
3. Honor a store-specific `runroot` in rootless mode (or namespace the
   runroot by graphroot/store). The 5.4.2 `getRootlessStorageOpts` forcing
   `<runtime>/containers`, combined with the env-config reload discarding the
   configured value, is what creates the collision.
4. Do not swallow the real error in exec user lookup. Report
   `ENOENT <mountpoint>/etc/passwd` instead of `ErrNoPasswdEntries`, and
   consider resolving the user from the container's own root
   (`/proc/<pid>/root`) or the OCI spec rather than the host merged path.

## Workarounds

- Give the alternate store a private runroot. On current main, a distinct
  `runroot` in `storage.conf` is enough. On 5.4.2, pass
  `podman --runroot=<distinct>` for a *fresh* store; existing store databases
  reject it with `database run root ... does not match our run root ...:
  database configuration mismatch`.
- Do not run any default-store command (including `podman unshare`) between
  the alternate-store build and the exec. The first exec then succeeds, but
  the store stays broken for the next command, so this is only a race
  workaround.
- `podman restart` and `podman system migrate` do not help (restart fails,
  migrate kills the container).

# Podman #30006 is still reproducible on current Podman (6.3.0-dev)

## TL;DR

The original reproducer no longer fails on current main because
`CONTAINERS_STORAGE_CONF` is now parsed directly and an explicit `runroot` in
the alternate config is honored. The underlying bug is still present: the
overlay mount registry (`mountpoints.json`) lives under the *runroot*, not under
the store, so any two rootless stores that share a runroot can overwrite each
other's mount records. When the alternate store does that, the next default-store
command lazily unmounts the running container's merged rootfs, and user lookup
fails with:

    Error: unable to find user app: no matching entries in passwd file

A reproducer that still triggers this on current main is provided at
`trigger-issue30006-recent.sh`.

## Versions tested

- Debian 13 (trixie), kernel 6.12, cgroup v2, systemd 257
- Rootless user, uid 1000, `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/run/user/1000`
- podman 5.4.2+ds1-2+b2 (original report) -> reproduced
- podman built from current main `c1d4564f03` -> `6.3.0-dev`,
  go.podman.io/storage v1.65.1-0.20261105174844-179286b8f253 -> reproduced
  with the new trigger below
- crun 1.21, conmon from Debian

## What changed on current main

On 5.4.2, rootless `getRootlessStorageOpts()` unconditionally overwrote the
runroot with `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/containers`, and the alternate config was reloaded
in a way that discarded its `runroot`/`graphroot`. That is why the original
two-store script collided.

On current main, `LoadStoreOptions` parses `CONTAINERS_STORAGE_CONF` through
`configfile.ParseTOML` (`EnvironmentName: "CONTAINERS_STORAGE_CONF"`,
`vendor/go.podman.io/storage/types/options.go:136-145`) and then applies
`storage.runroot` / `storage.graphroot` from that file
(`options.go:225-253`). With the issue's explicit
`runroot=$PODMAN_HOME/1`, the alternate store now gets its own registry, so the
original script does not fail.

## The remaining bug

The per-store mount registry is still keyed only by the runroot:

- `runhome := filepath.Join(options.RunRoot, filepath.Base(home))`
  (`drivers/overlay/overlay.go:341`)
- `rlpath := filepath.Join(s.runRoot, driverPrefix+"layers")`
  (`store.go:1190-1191`) -> `<runroot>/overlay-layers`
- `mountspath()` -> `<runroot>/overlay-layers/mountpoints.json`
  (`layers.go:905-907`)

The save path is destructive:

- `loadMounts()` clears all local `MountPoint`/`MountCount` and only applies
  records whose layer ID exists in the *current* store (`layers.go:1109-1145`).
  Records from another store are silently ignored.
- `saveMounts()` writes only the current store's layers with
  `MountCount > 0` (`layers.go:1244-1275`), replacing the whole file. A store
  that knows nothing about the other store's running container writes `[]`.

Then, in the store that owns the container:

1. On the next command, `loadMounts()` reads `[]`, so the container's layer has
   `MountCount == 0`.
2. `store.Shutdown()` decides no layer is mounted and calls
   `graphDriver.Cleanup()` (`store.go:3894`, `store.go:3948-3957`).
3. `overlay.Cleanup()` does `mount.Unmount(d.home)` ->
   `umount2(<graphroot>/overlay, MNT_DETACH)` (`overlay.go:907-912`).
4. Rootless podman runs inside the pause process's mount namespace, so the
   container's `<graphroot>/overlay/<id>/merged` mount disappears with the
   driver-home bind mount.
5. `podman exec --user app` tries to read `<mountpoint>/etc/passwd`; the missing
   file is reported by moby/sys/user as `ErrNoPasswdEntries`, hence the
   misleading "no matching entries in passwd file" message.

The container itself keeps running. `--user 0` still works (numeric UID needs no
passwd lookup), `podman ps` still shows it as Up, and the payload's own mount
namespace still has the overlay at `/`.

## Reproducer for current main

The key difference from the original issue script: the alternate store omits
`runroot`, so it inherits the default `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/containers`. That
recreates the shared registry on current main.

```ini
[storage]
driver = "overlay"
rootless_storage_path = "<workdir>/alt/store"
```

`trigger-issue30006-recent.sh` does the following:

1. Builds a base image with a user `app` and starts `t1` in the default store.
2. Builds the alternate store's config without `runroot`; verifies its runroot
   equals the default one; exits 3 with an explanation if it does not.
3. Seeds the alternate store with `podman save` / `podman load`, so the later
   alternate build needs no network.
4. Runs `podman exec --user app` (baseline: succeeds).
5. Builds `FROM issue30006-base` + `RUN true` with `CONTAINERS_STORAGE_CONF`
   pointing at the alternate config -> `mountpoints.json` becomes `[]`.
6. Runs `podman ps` in the default store to force `Shutdown()`/`Cleanup()`.
7. Runs `podman exec --user app` (expected: fails).
8. Checks `podman exec --user 0` and that `t1` is still Up.

Usage, as a normal rootless user in one shell (not root):

```bash
PODMAN=/path/to/podman ./trigger-issue30006-recent.sh /tmp/issue30006
```

Exit codes: `0` reproduced, `1` not reproduced, `2` wrong environment,
`3` alternate store got a private runroot. `BASE_IMAGE` and `PODMAN` are
overridable; `PODMAN_TEST_SKIP_CLEANUP=1` keeps the broken container.

## Observed evidence on 6.3.0-dev

Before the alternate build:

    mountpoints.json: [{"id":"<layer>","path":".../merged","count":1}]
    pause mount ns: overlay-home=1, <merged>=1

After the alternate build (before any default-store command):

    mountpoints.json: []
    pause mount ns: overlay-home=1, <merged>=1     # mounts exist, bookkeeping lost

After a plain `podman ps` in the default store:

    pause mount ns: overlay-home=0, <merged>=0
    t1: Up

Then:

    podman exec --user app t1 echo ...   -> rc=255
      Error: unable to find user app: no matching entries in passwd file
    podman exec --user 0 t1 id           -> rc=0, uid=0(root) ...
    podman ps                            -> t1 Up

The same script also reproduces on podman 5.4.2.

## Suggested fixes (unchanged)

1. Make the mount registry per-store rather than per-runroot, or merge on write
   instead of replacing the file with only the current store's layers.
2. Do not let `overlay.Cleanup()` unmount the driver home based on incomplete
   mount state, or only unmount what the current store/process owns.
3. Namespace the runroot by store/graphroot, or make rootless defaults not
   silently coalesce multiple stores onto one runroot.
4. Do not swallow the `ENOENT` from `<mountpoint>/etc/passwd`; report it instead
   of `ErrNoPasswdEntries`, and consider resolving the user from the container's
   own root (`/proc/<pid>/root`) or the OCI spec.

## Workaround

- Give each rootless store a private `runroot` in its storage config. On current
  main this works for new stores. An existing store DB rejects a changed runroot
  with `database run root ... does not match ...` (`podman --runroot=...`).
- Do not run any default-store command between the alternate-store write and the
  exec; the first exec usually still succeeds. This is only a race workaround;
  the registry stays corrupted for the next command.
- `podman restart` still fails with the same user-lookup error, and
  `podman system migrate` stops/kills the container. Neither recovers it.

## Separate note for Debian testing

On this Debian 13 system, `/usr/share/containers/storage.conf` has uncommented
root paths:

    runroot = "/run/containers/storage"
    graphroot = "/var/lib/containers/storage"

Current podman honors them even for uid 1000, so a freshly built binary fails
with `mkdir /var/lib/containers/storage: permission denied`. The reproducer was
run with a clean rootless config:

    [storage]
    driver = "overlay"
    rootless_storage_path = "/home/<user>/.../store"

That packaging issue is independent of #30006, but it can mask the reproducer on
Debian.

## Appendix: reproducer script

Save as `trigger-issue30006-recent.sh`, `chmod +x`, and run as a rootless user.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#
# Trigger the failure mode of containers/podman#30006 on recent Podman.
#
# Why the original reproducer no longer fails everywhere
# ------------------------------------------------------
# Podman 5.4.x rootless forced every store to runroot=$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/containers
# even when an alternate CONTAINERS_STORAGE_CONF set a different `runroot`.  So an
# alternate store and the default store shared
#
#     $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/containers/overlay-layers/mountpoints.json
#
# Recent Podman honors `runroot` from the alternate config, so the original script
# (which sets runroot=$PODMAN_HOME/1) now gives the alternate store a private
# registry and does not collide.
#
# The hazard is still there whenever two rootless stores *share* a runroot:
# `mountpoints.json` is keyed by the runroot only, so the last store to write it
# replaces the other store's mount records with its own (usually []).
#
# This script creates that condition in the most realistic way: the alternate
# config sets only `rootless_storage_path` and omits `runroot`, so rootless Podman
# falls back to the default $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/containers -- the same runroot as the
# default store.
#
# Failure chain
# -------------
#   1. t1 runs in the default store; mountpoints.json records its mounted layer.
#   2. an alternate-store build (a write) rewrites the shared file without t1.
#   3. the next default-store command sees MountCount==0, calls
#      store.Shutdown() -> overlay.Cleanup() -> unmount(<graphroot>/overlay,
#      MNT_DETACH) inside the pause mount namespace, which also detaches the
#      container's <merged> mount.
#   4. `podman exec --user app` cannot open <mountpoint>/etc/passwd; moby/sys/user
#      reports that missing file as ErrNoPasswdEntries:
#          unable to find user app: no matching entries in passwd file
#
# The container stays Up; `podman exec --user 0` still works (numeric UID needs no
# passwd entry).
#
# Usage
# -----
#   ./trigger-issue30006-recent.sh [WORKDIR]
#
# Run as a normal rootless user, not root, in a single shell.  The script exits 0
# when the bug is reproduced and 1 when it is not.  Workdir defaults to
# ./issue30006-recent.  Cleanup of the alternate store may need root afterwards
# (its files are owned by the subuid range).
#
# Environment overrides:
#   BASE_IMAGE=ubuntu:latest        image used to build the test image
#   PODMAN=podman                   podman binary to test (e.g. ./bin/podman)
#   PODMAN_TEST_SKIP_CLEANUP=1      keep the broken t1 container for inspection

set -u

PODMAN=${PODMAN:-podman}
BASE_IMAGE=${BASE_IMAGE:-ubuntu:latest}
KEEP=${PODMAN_TEST_SKIP_CLEANUP:-0}

if [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "ERROR: run this as a normal (rootless) user; root uses a different store." >&2
    exit 2
fi

export XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/run/user/$(id -u)}
if [ ! -d "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR" ]; then
    echo "ERROR: XDG_RUNTIME_DIR ($XDG_RUNTIME_DIR) does not exist." >&2
    exit 2
fi

BASE=${1:-$PWD/issue30006-recent}
ALT_STORE="$BASE/alt/store"
ALT_CONF="$BASE/alt/storage.conf"
ALT_TMP="$BASE/alt/tmp"

step()  { printf '\n=== %s ===\n' "$*"; }
die()   { echo "ERROR: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
pw()    { "$PODMAN" "$@"; }

pause_pid() {
    find "$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR" -type f -name pause.pid 2>/dev/null | head -1 | xargs -r cat 2>/dev/null
}

# count mount table entries for an exact mount point in the pause mount namespace
mount_count() {
    local path=$1 p
    p=$(pause_pid)
    [ -n "${p:-}" ] || { echo "?"; return; }
    grep -Fc " $path " "/proc/$p/mountinfo" 2>/dev/null || true
}

show_state() {
    local p
    p=$(pause_pid)
    echo "pause=${p:-none}"
    echo "  default graphroot/overlay mounts: $(mount_count "$DEFAULT_OVERLAY")"
    echo "  t1 merged mounts:                 $(mount_count "$MERGED")"
    if [ -r "$MPJ" ]; then
        echo "  mountpoints.json: $(cat "$MPJ")"
    else
        echo "  mountpoints.json: <missing>"
    fi
}

step "0. prepare $BASE"
rm -rf "$BASE" 2>/dev/null || true
mkdir -p "$BASE" "$BASE/alt/store" "$BASE/alt/tmp" "$BASE/tmp"
# Use a user-owned temp dir.  With some distro configs the default /var/tmp
# makes rootless pasta fail to create its pid file.
TMPDIR="$BASE/tmp"
export TMPDIR
cd "$BASE" || exit 1
if [ "$KEEP" = "1" ]; then
    echo "PODMAN_TEST_SKIP_CLEANUP=1: t1 will be kept for inspection."
else
    trap 'pw rm -f t1 >/dev/null 2>&1 || true' EXIT
fi

# Make sure the test starts from a clean container name.
pw rm -f t1 >/dev/null 2>&1 || true

if [ "$(pw info --format '{{.Host.Security.Rootless}}' 2>/dev/null)" != "true" ]; then
    die "podman is not running rootless (or is remote)."
fi

DEFAULT_RUNROOT=$(pw info --format '{{.Store.RunRoot}}') || die "podman info failed"
DEFAULT_GRAPHROOT=$(pw info --format '{{.Store.GraphRoot}}') || die "podman info failed"
DEFAULT_DRIVER=$(pw info --format '{{.Store.GraphDriverName}}') || die "podman info failed"
if [ "$DEFAULT_DRIVER" != "overlay" ]; then
    die "this reproducer needs the overlay storage driver (current: $DEFAULT_DRIVER)."
fi
DEFAULT_OVERLAY="$DEFAULT_GRAPHROOT/overlay"
echo "default store: graphroot=$DEFAULT_GRAPHROOT runroot=$DEFAULT_RUNROOT"

step "1. build the test image in the default store"
cat > Dockerfile.base <<EOF
FROM $BASE_IMAGE
RUN useradd -m app || adduser -D app
USER app
EOF
if ! pw build --network=none -t issue30006-base -f Dockerfile.base .; then
    die "could not build the test image (base image: $BASE_IMAGE)"
fi

step "2. create the alternate store (no runroot -> inherits the shared rootless runroot)"
cat > "$ALT_CONF" <<EOF
[storage]
driver = "overlay"
rootless_storage_path = "$ALT_STORE"
EOF

# Seed the alternate store with the test image so the later build needs no network.
# This happens before t1 exists, so any mount-registry write here is harmless.
pw save -o base.tar issue30006-base || die "podman save failed"
if ! CONTAINERS_STORAGE_CONF="$ALT_CONF" TMPDIR="$ALT_TMP" \
        pw load -i base.tar; then
    die "podman load into the alternate store failed"
fi
rm -f base.tar

ALT_RUNROOT=$(CONTAINERS_STORAGE_CONF="$ALT_CONF" TMPDIR="$ALT_TMP" \
    pw info --format '{{.Store.RunRoot}}') || die "alternate podman info failed"
ALT_GRAPHROOT=$(CONTAINERS_STORAGE_CONF="$ALT_CONF" TMPDIR="$ALT_TMP" \
    pw info --format '{{.Store.GraphRoot}}') || die "alternate podman info failed"
echo "alternate store: graphroot=$ALT_GRAPHROOT runroot=$ALT_RUNROOT"

if [ "$ALT_RUNROOT" != "$DEFAULT_RUNROOT" ]; then
    cat >&2 <<EOF
ERROR: the alternate store did not inherit the default runroot, so it has a
       private mount registry and this script cannot trigger the bug.

       default runroot:   $DEFAULT_RUNROOT
       alternate runroot: $ALT_RUNROOT

       If this is a Podman version/config that forces a private runroot, set the
       alternate config's runroot to "$DEFAULT_RUNROOT" explicitly and retry.
EOF
    exit 3
fi

MPJ="$DEFAULT_RUNROOT/overlay-layers/mountpoints.json"

step "3. run t1 in the default store"
mkdir -p 123
pw run -d --name t1 --replace --userns=keep-id \
    -v "$PWD/123:/tmp:Z,U" issue30006-base sleep 600 || die "podman run failed"
sleep 2

UPPER=$(pw inspect t1 --format '{{.GraphDriver.Data.UpperDir}}') || die "inspect failed"
MERGED="${UPPER%/diff}/merged"
echo "merged=$MERGED"

step "4. exec as app before the alternate build (expected: works)"
if ! pw exec --user app t1 echo ">>> step 4 OK"; then
    die "baseline exec failed; the test cannot continue"
fi
show_state

step "5. write to the alternate store (build) -- clobbers the shared mount registry"
cat > alt/Dockerfile <<EOF
FROM issue30006-base
RUN true
EOF
if ! CONTAINERS_STORAGE_CONF="$ALT_CONF" TMPDIR="$ALT_TMP" \
        pw build --network=none --pull=never \
        -t issue30006-alt -f alt/Dockerfile .; then
    die "alternate-store build failed"
fi
show_state

step "6. next default-store command -- triggers Shutdown()/overlay.Cleanup()"
pw ps --format '{{.Names}} {{.Status}}' || true
show_state

step "7. exec as app (expected: failure)"
OUT=$(pw exec --user app t1 echo ">>> step 7 OK" 2>&1)
RC=$?
echo "$OUT"
echo "rc=$RC"

step "8. control checks"
pw exec --user 0 t1 id || echo "(exec --user 0 also failed)"
pw ps --format '{{.Names}} {{.Status}}' || true

step "result"
if [ "$RC" -ne 0 ] && printf '%s' "$OUT" | grep -q 'no matching entries in passwd file'; then
    echo "PASS: issue #30006 reproduced (exec --user app failed after the alternate-store write)."
    echo "Artifacts left in: $BASE"
    if [ "$KEEP" = "1" ]; then
        echo "t1 kept for inspection:"
        echo "  $PODMAN inspect t1 --format '{{.GraphDriver.Data.UpperDir}}'"
        echo "  $PODMAN exec --user 0 t1 id"
    fi
    echo "The alternate store is owned by the subuid range; remove it as root if needed:"
    echo "  sudo rm -rf '$BASE'"
    exit 0
fi

echo "FAIL: the expected passwd-lookup error was not observed."
echo "State:"
show_state
exit 1
```
